title: Measure the failure on the portal, and record what it showed
question: can a lazily loaded route's chunk be made to fail on the Insurance Portal without a page-side edit, and what does the panel surface render when it does?

verdict.statement: On the Insurance Portal a lazily loaded route's chunk can be made to fail with no page-side edit: while the router was asked to activate the `contract` route, the browser's own request interception failed its chunk `src-YWNMU5GU.js`, the dynamic import rejected with `Failed to fetch dynamically imported module: http://localhost:4507/src-YWNMU5GU.js`, the router stayed on `/home`, and the page kept rendering the home route with no error surface. The portal does not produce the record this milestone renders from: the page states no import specifier — the served initial chunk calls the route's `import()` with the emitted chunk URL, which extension/import-failure.js refuses to read back as a specifier — and no module ships the tap that publishes `importAttempts`. The panel surface therefore answers `cannot-tell`, never an import, a route path, a status, a hash or a version drift.
portalLacks: the import specifier the route's import() was called with, as this record takes one
the attempt record itself — the `importAttempts` entry the panel renders

surface.why: the record the portal carries is absent — the capture measured `window.angularAiImportFailure` as `undefined` and found no `importAttempts` — and an absent record is `cannot-tell` with `record-unreadable`, while an empty one is `cannot-tell` with `no-import-recorded`. Neither reading names a specifier, a route path, a status or a hash, because the record carries none.

produced.artefact: a failed dynamic import on a lazily loaded route
produced.evidence: both arms: the router's navigation promise rejected with "TypeError: Failed to fetch dynamically imported module: http://localhost:4507/src-YWNMU5GU.js"

produced.artefact: a response status for that request, when one arrived
produced.evidence: arm fulfilled-404 recorded `status: 404`; arm aborted recorded no response and the failure "net::ERR_FAILED"

produced.artefact: the route whose lazy load produced it
produced.evidence: the router's own config names `contract` with a `loadChildren`, and `ɵgetLoadedRoutes` reports it unloaded after the failure

lacking.artefact: the import specifier the route's import() was called with, as this record takes one
lacking.why: the page states only the emitted chunk URL: the served initial chunk rewrites the route's `import('@ng-journal/contract/routes')` to `import("/src-YWNMU5GU.js")`, and a chunk URL is exactly the value extension/import-failure.js refuses to read back as a specifier. The source-level specifier exists in the portal's own route table and nowhere in the running page.

lacking.artefact: the attempt record itself — the `importAttempts` entry the panel renders
lacking.why: nothing publishes one. extension/import-failure.js is not listed in extension/manifest.json, so no content script loads it, and the page carries neither `angularAiImportFailure` nor `importAttempts`. The tap the record describes is the caller's, and at this head no caller installs it for the `contract` route or for any other route the portal loads.

citations.text: // navigation and hands it each attempt the router's import returned; it writes the answer for that

fixture.why: the portal carries a lazily loaded route — `contract` — and the capture failed that route's chunk, so the fallback the intent allows for a portal with no such route is not the case here: a fixture would repeat the same measurement on another app. It would also not supply the artefact the portal lacks, because src-YWNMU5GU.js names a compiled chunk there too.
wouldNeedToSupply: a route whose lazy load the record can name a specifier for, i.e. a route the record states as `{ specifier, routePath, outcome }` rather than one whose compiled `import()` argument is a chunk URL

the tap itself: something in the extension (not in the inspected page) has to hand `extension/import-failure.js` each attempt the router made, because no module in extension/manifest.json loads it and the page states no attempt
a page whose failing request the browser can fail on purpose, which the portal already is — so a fixture verdict would have to be justified by the two artefacts above, not by the failure

manifest.note: the manifest is the list of scripts a content script loads, so a zero here is the measurement that this milestone's record module is not shipped into any page at this head

routeSource.note: the portal is a checkout of its own repository, so this line is resolved when that checkout is present and named absent when it is not

capture.reads: the portal is served by control-angular-dev-app and one page is driven through a control-ai-browsers instance by playwright-cli `run-code`: three probes, one discovery and two arms, each returning its own readings. The served initial chunk is fetched once from the dev server to state what specifier the compiled route closure passes to `import()`. The join is then run in a bare `node:vm` context over the record the portal carries.
capture.reading: an armed run re-derives every fact above and writes the file only when a byte moved, so two armed runs in a row are byte-identical; a default run writes nothing, re-derives the join's answers, the manifest scan, the module citation and the portal route source, and hashes the record before and after to prove the bytes did not move.

environment.browser: the control-ai-browsers instance chrome-beta-nano (Chrome Beta), driven by playwright-cli
environment.note: the probes called `window.ng.ɵgetRouterInstance` and `window.ng.ɵnavigateByUrl`, which answer only in a development build; the portal flow's process table, evidence directory and logs are the skill's bookkeeping for `down` and stay in its evidence directory, so only the facts this record uses are carried here
